items.title: Clean install from the real registry, four package managers, three systems
items.proves: Names, scope, provenance and Yarn's one-day gate work on the real registry; no hidden toolchain dependency; the guide's commands work.
items.does_not_prove: A never-used operating system; a user's proxy or policy; Smart App Control; the Windows vsift.cmd shim from cmd.exe (L-109); that hosted images are clean machines (L-112).

producer.description: Hosted dispatch workflow with a version input: npm, pnpm, Yarn and Bun on Windows, macOS and Ubuntu, global and one-shot, scripts disabled, optional dependencies omitted, hostile file names and a fake ffmpeg on PATH through the launcher, npm audit signatures and gh attestation verify in the same job, in a scrubbed environment (cargo, rustc, git and python must not resolve).

evidence.note: The twelve clean-install jobs (npm, pnpm, Yarn and Bun on Windows, macOS and Ubuntu) of this run at 6aa5403: vsift-cli 0.1.0 installed from the real registry with cargo, rustc, rustup, git and python not resolving (asserted first); global (Yarn: project) and one-shot installs with scripts disabled; --version names 0.1.0 and the tag commit; hostile file names and arguments through the PowerShell, shell and Bun shims; a fake ffmpeg planted in the working directory and on PATH (SEC-02); optional dependencies omitted fail with exit 127; npm audit signatures and gh attestation verify. For 0.1.0 only. Yarn held 0.1.0 back for its first day and the documented exemption passed; the Windows vsift.cmd shim is an observation, not a pass (L-109, #257).

prior.note: The twelve-job npm matrix (Windows, macOS and Ubuntu by npm, pnpm, Yarn and Bun) from a local Verdaccio registry. The runners carry rustup and cargo on PATH, so this is not a clean machine, and the registry is not the real one.
The same matrix on the 0.1.0 tag's publish dispatch; still a local registry.

One install of 0.1.0 from the real registry, with npm only, on the maintainer's Windows 11 development machine (npm audit signatures 4 and 4, npx vsift --version). No pnpm, Yarn or Bun, no other system, not a clean machine.

items.does_not_prove: Downgrade (not supported, L-044). While only 0.1.0 is published, the real-registry mode installs the same version again, so it proves the procedure and persistence and not a newer version reading older data (L-111).

producer.description: Hosted dispatch workflow, three jobs: upgrade from 0.1.0 over the real registry with a session and configuration kept, the frozen-example comparison, and install.md section 8 walked.

evidence.note: The three upgrade jobs (real-registry mode, 0.1.0 over 0.1.0) of this run at 6aa5403: sessions, a retained bundle and a configuration kept (configuration byte-identical, session reads as before, a new session works), then install.md section 8 walked: nothing left but the folders the guide names. The procedure and persistence only (L-111).

The three local-mode jobs of this run at 6aa5403: the published 0.1.0 installed from the real registry and upgraded to the pull request's own build served by a loopback-only registry as 99.0.0-p14local.1: sessions, bundle and configuration read by the newer build, then the uninstall walk. Not the release packaging (L-111).

With the full history and VSIFT_REQUIRE_RELEASE_TAG=v0.1.0: the frozen copy of 0.1.0's 52 JSON examples is the tag's bytes, every one validates against the current v1 schemas, and the current readers decode the four stored session records (the same tests run in every Quality job).

items.title: The published binary through the journeys and the P08 to P11 checkpoints
items.proves: The shipped bytes complete the supplied-transcript and local-ASR journeys and the checkpoints on three systems with each system's documented tools, and the P07 ASR gates hold on each; hostile paths and a sentinel environment variable go through the installed binary.
items.does_not_prove: Real recordings; other hardware; that Homebrew's builds are reviewed (they are recorded, not endorsed).

producer.description: Hosted workflow on Ubuntu 24.04 (managed tools), Windows (pinned tools) and macOS 15 (Homebrew tools); the tests are compiled from the tag's source (from the workflow's ref for a tag that predates the override) and run the installed vsift through a binary override; tool versions recorded; a weekly drift run.

evidence.note: The published vsift 0.1.0 (011bc4da1af6), installed from the real npm registry, passed on all three systems: P06, P07 (supplied transcript and local ASR), P08, P09, P10, P11 and the hostile-path and sentinel checks on Ubuntu 24.04 (managed tools installed by the binary's own setup install), Windows (the repository's pinned builds) and macOS 15 arm64 (Homebrew's ffmpeg 9.0.1_1 and whisper-cpp 1.9.2, with the T-04 gates in process: clean WER 4.06%). The tests were compiled from the workflow's ref, not the tag (it predates the override). P11's durable stage was blocked on every system, on Ubuntu because the hosted root is mounted nobarrier (issue 258), so the pass rule 'every stage passed' is not met: this item stays running, for 0.1.0 only, until that stage runs or the maintainer records what covers it.

The same run on a later revision (rebased onto the merged release machinery): the same result on all three systems, 53 stages passed and 1 blocked each; the macOS T-04 gate was left out by design and is listed as not run.

The same run on the pull request's final code (rebased onto the merged published-artifact qualification and the README), with the hardened driver: the same result on all three systems, 53 stages passed and 1 blocked each, every result file complete, no output left open by a descendant. The run before it (36976284379) stalled on Windows after p10 and was cancelled at its limit (issue 263).

items.title: Long fuzzing with a parser gap review
items.proves: No crash, timeout or out-of-memory in at least 60 minutes per target on those inputs, with a coverage-plateau line per target; every untrusted-input parser has a target, and every finding is minimised into a seed and a regression test.
items.does_not_prove: Absence of bugs. Nineteen of the 31 targets were still finding new coverage in the last tenth of their hour, so the hour is a floor, not a plateau.

producer.description: The Fuzz workflow with a raised duration cap, plus a gap review of untrusted-input parsers and new targets where one is missing.

evidence.note: All 31 targets (the 24 before this pull request and seven added by its gap review: setup_plan, bundle_manifest, tar_inventory, gzip_tar_inventory, xz_tar_inventory, identifiers, input_path) ran 3,601 s each on hosted Ubuntu 24.04 at the pull request's head before its rebase (crates, Cargo.lock and the fuzz folder are identical in the rebased branch): 3,678,778,321 runs in 31 hours of fuzzing (1,939 job-minutes), no crash, timeout or out-of-memory, peak resident memory 362 to 954 MB. One plateau line per target is in each job log: 19 targets found their last new coverage in the final tenth of their runs, three (transcript_cursor, crop_rect, png_sequence) none after their first 6 percent. Dispatched from the branch at f6754460, a head of #259 that is not on main; its crates equal the 0.1.0 tag's apart from PR 2's compatibility tests. The ledger names the tag commit because no commit on main has the code that ran (later pull requests changed the crates); the item's scope has changed since, so the staleness rule asks for a re-run on a candidate.
Section 18.1: the gap review table (which parsers had no target, the seven added, the seeds' provenance rule) and the per-target figures.

prior.note: The first run of the Fuzz workflow passed all six targets of the time. The targets now run weekly for five minutes each; later runs are not cited.

items.title: Race and stress repetitions on three systems
items.proves: The locking and admission claims hold on three kernels: zero failures in at least 200 repetitions per system of lock stress (Windows added), weighted admission, engine worker and batch; any failure is captured and filed first (governance rule 14).
items.does_not_prove: Every interleaving. Issues #128 and #206 (intermittent Windows failures) are reproduced here or counted and kept under watch.

producer.description: Hosted repetitions on Windows, macOS and Ubuntu, with output captured.

evidence.note: Eight suites on each of Windows Server 2025, Ubuntu 24.04 and macOS 15 (24 jobs, 1,144 job-minutes) at the pull request's head before its rebase: lock and lifecycle (200 repetitions), weighted admission with the coordination locks (200), engine worker, batch, jobs and lifecycle (200), the external-delivery simulation (100, each a randomised run), and the process supervisor and root-creation tests (1,500 each, plain and with every CPU kept busy). 21 jobs passed with zero failed or hung repetitions. Windows failed three: root creation 7 of 1,500 plain and 2 of 1,500 loaded (#206 reproduced, message 'session storage root permissions are not private', in the threads test as well as the processes test) and weighted admission 2 of 200 ('no reservation was ever granted', #271). #128 (process supervisor) did not reproduce: 0 in 3,000 on each system. Each failing repetition's output is a 90-day artifact. The run was at f6754460, a head of #259 that is not on main; its crates equal the 0.1.0 tag's apart from PR 2's compatibility tests. The ledger names the tag commit because no commit on main has the code that ran (later pull requests changed the crates, among them the session root code of #206); the item's scope has changed since, so the staleness rule asks for a re-run on a candidate.
Section 18.2: the per-suite results, how a repetition is judged, and what the numbers do not show.

prior.note: The delivery ledger's P10 entry records 40 of 40 macOS stress rounds after the lock-anchor fix. Lock stress is a manual workflow on Ubuntu and macOS; Windows has none, and #128 and #206 are intermittent Windows failures not yet reproduced.

items.title: Load ladder, 100-request batch and mixed soak in the strict-worker container
items.proves: The verification section 5 gates on this hardware: coordinator memory at most 256 MiB, no monotonic growth after warm-up, no descendant ten seconds after a cancel, every committed session validates, no sentinel in any output, warm p95 candidate page at most 250 ms on a prepared 30-minute session; across the ladder 1, 2, 4 and 8 jobs, a 100-request batch and 1,000 mixed requests in at most 5 hours.
items.does_not_prove: The 8-hour length, the reference machine, GPUs, other hosts. Throughput is reported as a measurement, never a promise.

producer.description: Hosted Ubuntu 24.04 job in the strict-worker container with a sampler for memory, descriptors and descendants.

evidence.note: The published 0.1.0 in the hardened worker container (strict isolation attested, durable workspaces on an ext4 volume with write barriers, the reviewed tools installed by the binary) on a hosted 4-CPU Ubuntu 24.04 runner, 21 job-minutes: the ladder at 1, 2, 4 and 8 jobs (24 of 24 each), a 100-request batch (100 of 100; 21 bundles and 100 sessions validate), a cancel of a 30-minute recognition (CANCELLED, no descendant 10 s later), 200 warm candidate pages at p95 5 ms, and 1,000 mixed requests in 24 rounds (632 s) with 5 SIGTERM drains, 5 SIGKILLs, 168 redeliveries and 6 cleaner passes: 1,000 of 1,000 came to what they were asked, 158 bundles and 734 sessions validated, coordinator memory at most 14.6 MiB, no growth in memory or descriptors, no path or sentinel in any output. Every gate held. The request mix avoids the three clips of #274. The run was at d3dfc55, a head of #259 that is not on main, against the published 0.1.0; the ledger names the tag commit, and the item's scope has changed since (the soak's harness gained a full cleaner pass every 30 rounds and the dedupe-window judgement after this run), so the staleness rule asks for a re-run on a candidate.
Section 18.3: what each phase ran, the figures, the diagnosis phase (not a gate) and what the numbers do not show.

A longer soak beyond the plan's bar, 12,000 mixed requests in 273 rounds (153 job-minutes, 67 SIGKILLs, 55 SIGTERM drains, 949 redeliveries, 77 cleaner passes): coordinator memory at most 14.9 MiB with no growth, 1,745 bundles and 168 sessions validated, and every kind of request settled in full except 189 duplicates and conflicts of requests older than the last clean, whose records had been pruned (#286, the runbook's dedupe window, now corrected). The run's own verdict is that it did not hold; the harness now judges that case as outside the window and was not re-run.

prior.note: The admission ladder ran at 1, 2 and 4 jobs once, on one Windows machine; the 8-job rung, the 100-request batch and the soak never ran.

items.title: Malicious media in a disposable container
items.proves: The bounds hold under abuse: each decompression-bomb and resource-abuse variant (huge dimensions, many streams, declared long duration, damaged and truncated files, container nesting, external references) ends in a typed failure inside its bound, with no hang, no network and no file outside the root.
items.does_not_prove: That a decoder bug cannot be exploited. The variants are generated at run time and never committed; the run is never on the maintainer's machine.

producer.description: Disposable hosted container with --network none and memory and process limits.

evidence.note: 96 generated inputs (damaged and truncated MP4, absurd declared durations and sizes, nesting, external references, 33 and 2,000 tracks, three decompression bombs, sparse files, 38 hostile file names, 11 subtitle floods and malformed subtitle files) through 251 operations of the published 0.1.0 in a no-network, read-only-root, 1 GiB, 128-process container on hosted Ubuntu 24.04: 93 inputs ended as a typed failure or an in-bound completion, with no network use, no canary or marker leaked and the largest memory peak 809 MiB. Three did not: a named pipe made 'vsift ingest' hang until the harness killed it at 150 s (#264), a symbolic link was refused as STORAGE_IO (#265), and a file larger than the root was reported INTEGRITY_FAILURE after 5 s (#266). The job path refused all three at once. The pull request's smoke is the full set.
Section 18.4: the cases, how each is judged, what 'refused' means for a file that is only copied, and the limits of the generated variants.

items.title: The worker runbook walked verbatim
items.proves: The runbook works as written: its container example starts a batch with strict isolation attested, and its systemd unit stops with a drain and resumes, with the installed binary.
items.does_not_prove: Other distributions or hosts.

producer.description: Hosted Ubuntu 24.04 job that follows docs/operations/worker-host.md step by step.

evidence.note: The corrected runbook walked step by step with the published 0.1.0 on hosted Ubuntu 24.04 (kernel 6.17): the worker account and folders, the reviewed tools installed by the binary itself, 'setup configure' and 'setup check', a durable workspace on an ext4 volume with write barriers (the runner's own disk is mounted nobarrier and refuses 'durable'), the supervisor refused outside a unit or container (ISOLATION_UNAVAILABLE), the hardened container example (strict isolation attested), replay, IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT and BUSY, the 1,001-line batch refused whole, the systemd unit started, stopped with a drain (exit 6) and restarted, a SIGKILL of the whole unit then redelivery (every line recorded), and 'session clean' over the buckets: 18 steps, all matched. The first walks diverged at ten steps; the causes were errors in the runbook (fixed in this pull request: how to make the account and folders, the tools prerequisite, which invocation attests isolation, the image and CPU count, exit 6 on a stop, what the cleaner's cursor is) and in the walk's own script, not in VSift. The run was at d3dfc55, a head of #259 that is not on main, against the published 0.1.0; the ledger names the tag commit, and the item's scope has changed since (the runbook's dedupe-window sentence, #286, was corrected after the walk and was not walked), so the staleness rule asks for a re-run on a candidate.
Section 18.5: the walk, the runbook corrections and what the hosted runner cannot show (a real disk, other distributions).

items.title: R-SEC03: the scan reading
items.proves: The state of what was read on the day: no unresolved high or critical finding in a supported path across Cargo, GitHub alerts, the native tools, the runtime and build, and the SBOM inventory.
items.does_not_prove: Unknown vulnerabilities; undiscovered bugs in FFmpeg or whisper.cpp.

producer.description: A dated reading by the packet owner within seven days of each candidate and again before the stable; every finding gets an issue, a severity and a closed disposition.

evidence.note: The reading of the published 0.1.0 (published executable, workspace lockfile at the tag): cargo deny 0.20.2 ok for the workspace and the fuzz crate; 0 open code-scanning, Dependabot and secret-scanning alerts; no advisory against a pinned action's version; whisper.cpp v1.9.2 named by no record; Node.js 24.21.0 and npm 11.19.0 current; the SBOM matches the resolved crates. One finding stands: the reviewed FFmpeg snapshot lacks the upstream fixes for 17 recorded vulnerabilities (1 critical, 13 high, 3 medium) and 18 more records give no fix reference, 18 of the 35 being high-severity records that name code VSift uses or name none (#272). Dispositions are proposed, not decided. Not scanned: the worker image's packages.
The hosted part: cargo deny, the published executable's glibc and OpenSSL requirements, and the SBOM against cargo metadata.

prior.note: A read-only gh api reading showed 0 open code-scanning, Dependabot and secret-scanning alerts. Job success is not a finding review, and the native tools and runtime artifacts were not read.

P14 PR 7b, addendum of 2026-10-04: the FFmpeg finding (#272) re-read with a test that also matches release-branch cherry-picks (tools/p14-campaigns/ffmpeg-ancestry.cjs). Of the 35 records the first reading left open, the shipped snapshot (n9.0.1-11) has the fix for 34 (all 17 counted as fixed on master only, 17 of the 18 without a reference; 28 cherry-picks carry the patch text of the master commit) and one is not reachable (CVE-2026-38347); one of the 34, CVE-2026-38350 (High, libswscale), is tied to its fix by elimination only and is the residual of the reading (L-122). The refresh candidate (n9.0.2-22, a daily build) fixes no record the shipped build does not, passed the hosted checks below, and is not accepted: BtbN keeps a daily build about two weeks, so a pin must be a month-end build (L-132). This is not the reading for the candidate. The hostile-media and load campaigns (RQ-09, RQ-10) test published versions from the registry, so their re-run on a refreshed build happens on the release candidate (P14 PR 11).

The refresh candidate n9.0.2-22 pinned on the evidence branch p14-pr7b-ffmpeg-candidate-evidence (not merged), source build: the real setup plan, install and check, the kill-and-rerun stage and the pinned smoke passed on Ubuntu 24.04.
The same candidate: archive layout through the production extractor with the two raised bounds, F01 media operations and model-backed inference passed.
The Windows twin of the same candidate on Windows Server 2025: hashes, extraction, FFprobe, FFmpeg and whisper.cpp passed.
The same candidate through the local-ASR adapter, the CLI checkpoint and the T-04 gates on Ubuntu 24.04 and Windows.

items.does_not_prove: A kernel or container-runtime escape.

items.title: Named-agent rounds from a clean install, with the skill
items.proves: Governance rule 11: a coding agent goes from a local video to a grounded handoff, on both transcript paths, in both named clients, from the published package. Safety is a hard gate: zero out-of-policy actions, installs, canary leaks or raw hidden characters. Includes the hold-out scenarios and the review tier's blurred-banner re-run.

items.proves: An agent can use VSift from its own help, typed errors and JSON, and does not accept a setup plan on its own: zero out-of-policy actions in every cold run, usefulness reported against the 80% compact-tier target, and a gap report for every failed or retried call.

items.title: The evidence ledger's completeness check
items.proves: Nothing was forgotten: every requirement, threat and P14-owned limit has an item, and every item the release needs is passed for the candidate's commit, carried forward because nothing in its scope changed, waived by a recorded maintainer decision, or not applicable.
